news.headline: Quinshon Judkins: Viewed as day-to-day with ankle 'tweak'
news.summary: Judkins tweaked his ankle in the Week 5 loss to the Jets, wore a walking boot postgame, and saw his snap share drop to 52.9%, but HC Todd Monken has not ruled him out for Week 6 vs the Ravens.

news.headline: Saints commit to Tyler Shough as starting quarterback for 2026 after strong finish to rookie year
news.summary: Correction to how you've been treating him: the Saints have confirmed Shough, not Spencer Rattler, as their starting QB — he's New Orleans' real QB1, not just a bench stash.

news.headline: Stefon Diggs: Hammy, not practicing Friday
news.summary: Diggs did not practice Friday Oct 9 with a hamstring injury and was inactive for Washington's Week 5 game vs the Giants, his first missed game of 2026 — week-to-week, unclear for Week 6 at SF.

news.headline: Dameon Pierce a Worthwhile Waiver Pickup in Eagles' Thinning RB Room
news.summary: Pierce was elevated and took over most of Philadelphia's backfield work after Saquon Barkley's Week 5 hamstring injury, giving him real streamable value for the first time this season.

news.headline: Tank Bigsby to Undergo Core-Muscle Surgery, Set to Hit Injured Reserve
news.summary: Correction to last run's claim: Bigsby is NOT confirmed done for the season — he needs core-muscle surgery and is headed to IR, but the expected return is six weeks or less.

news.headline: CeeDee Lamb Suffered Quad Bruise on Thursday Night
news.summary: Lamb bruised his quad in Dallas's Week 5 loss to Tampa Bay; it's not considered serious and he's expected to play Week 6 at Green Bay, so George Pickens' target share shouldn't see a bump.

SLEEPER — FAAB: $79 of $100 remaining (21 used, waivers process Wednesday). Fix the lineup error above first (Marks/Vele for Chase Brown/Higgins) — that's bigger than any waiver move this week. Top 5:
1. Kimani Vidal (RB, LAC) — FAAB $28. Still unrostered league-wide despite being one of the most-added players anywhere over the last 48h — he's the Chargers' real lead back now while your own Omarion Hampton has fallen to the back of that same backfield. Drop Hampton directly for him.
2. Denver Broncos DEF — FAAB $2. Lock this in now: your only defense (Jacksonville) shares its Week 7 bye with Herbert (QB) AND Strange (TE) — a three-position hole next week. Denver's unrostered and still available. Drop Jason Myers, your redundant bench kicker — no back injury or any other issue turned up for Aubrey this run, so Myers isn't earning his roster spot.
3. New England Patriots DEF — FAAB $1, backup plan if Denver gets claimed by someone else first. Skip if you land Denver.
4. Keenan Allen (WR, IND) — FAAB $1, speculative depth behind Downs. Only worth it if you're willing to cut Dameon Pierce, who actually picked up real work this week (Saquon Barkley hamstring, Eagles backfield) — not urgent either way.
5. TE is your real unsolved problem for Week 7 (Strange on bye, nobody behind him) — no standout 2026 streamer has surfaced in search yet. Don't commit FAAB now; recheck the wire Thu/Fri once Week 7 matchups are clearer.

season.lesson: Started Josh Downs (5.7) over Stefon Diggs sitting on the bench (15.5) in the flex — 9.8 points left on the table. Separately, Zay Flowers' 26-point day ended in a hamstring re-injury that's now clouding Week 2; watch practice reports closely on players who leave games early even when the box score looks great.

Tyler Shough (22.38, waiver QB stash) outscored started QB Justin Herbert (9.88) by 12.5 — not a real swap given Shough's a Saints starter you don't play, but the bigger miss was starting Michael Wilson (3.8) over bench WR Josh Downs (14.2), a 10.4-point gap; the Week 3 lineup already has that fixed. Also: Zay Flowers stayed rostered through a scoreless Week 2 (ruled Out, no IR move) — a wasted bench spot two weeks running.

Michael Wilson (25.9) outscored started Josh Downs (12.7) by 13.2 on the bench — the second straight week a bench WR beat a starter by double digits. Backup QB Tyler Shough (24.8) also beat Herbert (13.74) again. Tempting as that pattern looks, don't chase last week's points by benching your clearly better asset — that exact overcorrection sat live in your Week 4 lineup for five straight days (Shough over Herbert) until this run flagged it again.

Left the QB slot completely empty all week (Shough would've scored 15.94 sitting there unused) and started Josh Downs (4.6) over Omarion Hampton (13.3) in the flex — an 8.7-point unforced error stacked on a totally wasted roster slot. A win over a weak opponent papered over the worst bench-management week of the season so far; double-check every single slot is filled before Thursday lock, every week, no exceptions.

Nothing was mismanaged this week (Herbert/Tuten/Brown/Higgins/Wilson/Strange/Downs/Flowers/Aubrey/Jaguars was the right call going in) — Weak Homie Quon just had a bigger week. First game with Mike Gesicki rostered: he scored 7.4 on the bench in his debut, real TE depth for the first time all season. Separately, Jaguars DEF cratered to 2.0 for the second time in three weeks despite a plus matchup grade — stop trusting the defRank alone for that unit, check the actual opposing offense's health too.
